title: Ind-quasi-affine effectivity for a labelled coproduct over an affine fpqc chart
statement:
Let $p:V\to X$ be a morphism of schemes with $V$ affine such that $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $S$ be any set in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], put $T=\coprod_{s\in S}V$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and equip $T/V$ with any scheme descent datum over $V/X$ [def-pd-descent-datum].

For every affine open $B\subseteq V$ and every quasi-compact open subscheme $K\subseteq T\times_VB=\coprod_SB$, there is a finite subset $J\subseteq S$ such that $K$ is contained as an open subscheme in the affine scheme $D=\coprod_JB$. For every affine open $B'\subseteq B$, the inverse image $K'=K\times_BB'$ is quasi-compact and open in the affine scheme $D'=\coprod_JB'$. In particular the morphism $K\to B$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], with a quasi-affine scheme meaning a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. The descent datum is effective: there exist an $X$-scheme $Y$ and an isomorphism $\eta:Y\times_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ over $V$ inducing the given datum. No finiteness of $S$, quasi-compactness of $T\to V$, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed; empty $S$ and empty $V$ are included.

proof.text: For an affine open $B\subseteq V$, the inverse image of the $s$th open component $V\subseteq T$ is its open restriction $B$: the open-subscheme description [def-weil-open-immersion] and fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identify this pullback, since a morphism into $V$ factors through $B$ exactly when its underlying image lies in $B$. These inverse images remain disjoint and cover the pullback. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] identifies $T\times_VB$ with $\coprod_SB$: the morphism from the latter is an isomorphism on each open component, and the componentwise inverses agree on the empty overlaps.

source.place: (2), labelled coproducts restricted to affine opens; elementary open-subscheme pullback calculation

proof.text: The component intersections $K\cap B_s$ form an open cover of $K$. By [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], finitely many suffice; let $J\subseteq S$ be their finite set of labels. The union of these components is the open subscheme $D=\coprod_JB$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], so the inclusion of $K$ factors as an open inclusion into $D$. Clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $D$ affine, including $J=\varnothing$ (the spectrum of the zero ring). Thus $K$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme.

source.place: (2), finite-component replacement for the infinite quasi-affine claim; finite subcover argument and finite affine coproduct

proof.text: For every affine open B' of B, the finite coproduct D' of copies of B' is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](4). The compact open K is quasi-affine because it is an open subscheme of the affine D. The affine base B is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus K -> B is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), and its base change to B' has compact source by clauses (2)--(3). The coproduct pullback of step 1 and pullback pasting identify this source with an open subscheme of D', with the same labels J. Compact open subschemes of affine schemes are quasi-affine, verifying [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] for K -> B.

source.place: Tag 0AP6, definition-ind-quasi-affine; relative quasi-affine-open criterion checked using finite components and affine quasi-separatedness

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-ind-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] with its covering $A\to B$ equal to $V\to X$ and its scheme over $A$ equal to $T\to V$. The covering is fpqc by the hypothesis. For every affine open of $V$, every quasi-compact open of its inverse image is quasi-affine over that affine open by steps 1--3. The given scheme descent datum is the required isomorphism with its cocycle. All hypotheses of the cited theorem thus hold; it gives the $X$-scheme $Y$ and the datum-compatible isomorphism $Y\times_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. The proof of steps 1--3 permits $J=\varnothing$ and arbitrary $S$. For $S=\varnothing$ or $V=\varnothing$ the same theorem still applies: its open condition is vacuous. No quasi-compactness of $T\to V$ or Noetherian assumption was used.

lean.statement: theorem coproduct_fpqc_effectivity {X V : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine V] (p : V ⟶ X) (hp : Presieve.singleton p ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage X) (S : Type v) [Small.{u} S] (D : Over.DescentDatum p (Over.mk (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)))) : (∀ (B : V.Opens), IsAffineOpen B → ∀ (K : (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι).Opens), IsCompact (K : Set (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι)) → ∃ (J : Finset S), IsAffine (∐ fun _ : J => B.toScheme) ∧ (∃ (j : K.toScheme ⟶ ∐ fun _ : J => B.toScheme), IsOpenImmersion j ∧ j ≫ Sigma.desc (fun s : J => B.ι ≫ Sigma.ι (fun _ : S => V) s.val) = K.ι ≫ pullback.fst (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι ∧ j ≫ Sigma.desc (fun _ : J => 𝟙 B.toScheme) = K.ι ≫ pullback.snd (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι ∧ (∀ (B' : B.toScheme.Opens), IsAffineOpen B' → IsAffine (∐ fun _ : J => B'.toScheme) ∧ CompactSpace (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) (K.ι ≫ pullback.snd (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι) B'.ι) ∧ ∃ (j' : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) (K.ι ≫ pullback.snd (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι) B'.ι ⟶ ∐ fun _ : J => B'.toScheme), IsOpenImmersion j' ∧ j' ≫ Sigma.desc (fun s : J => B'.ι ≫ Sigma.ι (fun _ : J => B.toScheme) s) = pullback.fst (K.ι ≫ pullback.snd (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι) B'.ι ≫ j ∧ j' ≫ Sigma.desc (fun _ : J => 𝟙 B'.toScheme) = pullback.snd (K.ι ≫ pullback.snd (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι) B'.ι)) ∧ IsQuasiAffineHom (K.ι ≫ pullback.snd (Sigma.desc (fun _ : S => 𝟙 V)) B.ι)) ∧ D.IsEffective
